entries.subject: NOIRLab iotw2127a (Dark Energy Camera, Dark Energy Survey)
entries.finding: The whole galaxy, 3383 x 3263 px over 14.82 x 14.30 arcmin (0.263 arcsec per pixel), CC BY 4.0. The page's centre, field and orientation hold: 72 of the 90 Gaia DR3 stars brighter than G = 19 in the frame have a star within 4 px, and a search over centre, scale, rotation and mirror finds nothing better than 73. The core is burned out.

entries.subject: ESO press images of NGC 1365
entries.finding: eso9920f (VLT FORS1) is 6.80 arcmin wide and eso1038a (HAWK-I, infrared) 6.50 arcmin, against an RC3 isophotal diameter of 11.2 arcmin: both cut the outer arms. potw1037a (Danish 1.5 m) holds the whole galaxy in 23.40 x 17.62 arcmin, but at 0.56 arcsec per pixel, half the resolution of the DECam image.
entries.revisitWhen: A sharper whole-disc photograph is published under an attribution licence.

entries.subject: Disc tilt and position angle
entries.finding: Leroy et al. (2021) give inclination 55.4 +/- 6.0 deg and position angle 201.1 +/- 7.5 deg. Lang et al. (2020) fit 55.4 deg and 210.7 deg to the CO velocity field, the same receding side; the PHANGS table's own row is used.
entries.revisitWhen: A kinematic fit with smaller errors is published.

entries.subject: Bulge
entries.finding: Salo et al. (2015), S4G Pipeline 4, table 7, NGC1365, model _bdbarfn: a Sérsic bulge (25.0% of the light, magnitude 10.204, half-light radius 12.64″ = 1.12 kpc, n = 0.857, axis ratio 0.577, PA 33.31°) and an exponential disc (53.8% of the light, scale length 95.05″ = 8.41 kpc, axis ratio 0.588, PA 31.66°, face-on central surface brightness 21.251, 20.674 as projected on the sky) and a Ferrers bar (14.3% of the light, radius 90.00″ = 7.97 kpc, axis ratio 0.504, PA 88.51°, central surface brightness 19.892 on the sky) and a point nucleus (7.0% of the light), which is neither bulge nor disc: its light stays on the flat picture. Used as published; the half-light surface brightness the bake needs, 17.74 mag per square arcsecond, follows from the bulge's magnitude, radius, index and axis ratio. At the disc's 55.4° the bulge's axis ratio is one an oblate spheroid in the disc plane can show (intrinsic 0.12).

entries.subject: Catalogued objects as dots
entries.finding: 34 dots from 2 published tables: 29 planetary nebulae (Scheuermann et al. (2022), CDS J/MNRAS/511/6087, 1,049 rows in the file); 5 supernova remnants (Scheuermann et al. (2022), CDS J/MNRAS/511/6087, 1,049 rows in the file). Each dot is a catalogued object at its published sky position, placed where its sight line meets the disc. Its height above the disc is drawn from a 1674 pc layer, the scale length over 7.3 ([Kregel et al. 2002](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0204154), [record](../../sources/kregel-2002-disc-flattening.json)); that height is not measured. Planetary nebulae near the centre can sit in the bulge, with the bulge's share of the fitted light there; that membership is drawn, not measured.

entries.subject: Ionised nebulae (Groves et al. 2023)
entries.finding: The table has rows for this galaxy, but CDS serves it per galaxy only through TAP, which answered with an error on 2026-10-03 (HTTP Error 503: Service Unavailable); the whole file is 43 MB. The dots follow when TAP answers.
